definition: The harness is all the software wrapped around an AI model: the tools it can reach, the permissions it has, the memory it keeps, and the app you talk to. The model is the brain; the harness is the body. Change the harness and the same model behaves like a completely different product.

edges.label: wraps around
edges.note: A harness can wrap any model — including DeepSeek.

example.body: Claude Desktop and a custom-built company harness can run the same underlying model, yet feel like different products. One team gives its assistant broad file access for engineers but locks it down for support staff — enforced by the harness through company sign-in and role switching, completely invisible to the model itself.
example.title: Same brain, different body

footnotes.body: A harness typically composes the system prompt, registers tool/MCP servers, enforces a permission policy (e.g. Okta OIDC with role switching), manages conversation memory and context assembly, and hooks up eval and logging.
footnotes.label: For the technical reader

name: Harness
tagline: Everything wrapped around the model — tools, permissions, memory — that turns a chatbot into a coworker.
whyItMatters: When an AI assistant feels surprisingly capable — or frustratingly limited — that's usually the harness, not the model. Two products running the same model can differ wildly in what they're allowed to do, and that difference is a design and governance choice.
